The widening of the confidence intervals across the horizons directly reflects the increasing uncertainty associated with longer-term predictions. While these intervals capture a significant range of probable outcomes, certain high-impact events could push the actual results outside these bounds. Conversely, a severe economic shock, a major geopolitical crisis, an unforeseen natural disaster, or a sharp and persistent negative shift in sentiment could drive the variable below 67.75. These "black swan" type events or fundamental shifts in the underlying drivers are inherently difficult to predict and fall outside the typical statistical variations accounted for in the confidence intervals.
